description: Composite two-panel figure of tensile properties for four heat-treatment conditions of Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr low-density steel. (a) is an engineering stress–strain plot with y-axis "Engineering Stress/MPa" (0–1200, ticks every 200) and x-axis "Engineering Strain/%" (0–60, ticks every 10); four solid curves are labelled MHT (black), S1000 (red), S1050 (blue) and S1100 (cyan), and a grey-shaded, unlabelled inset drawing of a tensile specimen occupies the lower-middle area. The red and blue curves form the highest plateau, near the 1000–1200 gridline midpoint; the black MHT curve is slightly lower and terminates at the lowest strain (~50%), whereas the cyan S1100 curve peaks just below the 1000 MPa gridline yet extends furthest, to ~60% strain. (b) plots "True Stress/Strain Hardening Rate/MPa" (0–2500) against "True Strain" (0.0–0.5); per the caption solid lines are true-stress curves and dashed lines strain-hardening-rate curves, and three roman-numbered regimes are marked: I (very low strain), II (roughly 0.1–0.3) and III (roughly 0.32–0.45). The hardening-rate curves are non-monotonic: after a steep drop at very low strain they rise to a hump peaking near 2000 MPa in regime II before declining in III. Together the panels compare strength–ductility trade-offs among S1000, S1050, MHT and S1100.

observations.observation: Panel (a) axes are labelled "Engineering Stress/MPa" (0–1200) and "Engineering Strain/%" (0–60).
Panel (a) legend contains four entries: MHT (black), S1000 (red), S1050 (blue) and S1100 (cyan).
In panel (a) the black MHT curve ends at the lowest strain (about 50%) while the cyan S1100 curve extends furthest (about 60%).
In panel (a) the red (S1000) and blue (S1050) curves occupy the highest plateau, between the 1000 and 1200 MPa gridlines, whereas the cyan S1100 curve peaks just below the 1000 MPa gridline.
Panel (b) axes are labelled "True Stress/Strain Hardening Rate/MPa" (0–2500) and "True Strain" (0.0–0.5), and the legend repeats the same four conditions (MHT, S1000, S1050, S1100).
Panel (b) contains three roman-numbered regions: I at very low strain, II at intermediate strain (roughly 0.1–0.3) and III at higher strain (roughly 0.32–0.45).
The dashed strain-hardening-rate curves in (b) are non-monotonic, showing a hump that peaks close to 2000 MPa in region II after the initial drop in region I.
A grey-shaded inset drawing of a tensile specimen appears in the lower-middle part of panel (a); it carries no legible axis or scale annotation.

The caption states that (a) is the engineering stress–strain curve and (b) the true stress–strain and strain work hardening rates for three different heat treatment processes, with solid and dashed lines denoting true stress and hardening rate respectively.
The caption says "three different heat treatment processes" while the plotted legend lists four conditions (MHT, S1000, S1050, S1100); caption and pixels disagree on the sample count.
The citing text states that YS and UTS decrease with increasing d_eff, with d_eff = 3.17 μm in S1000 and 3.84 μm in S1050, and that YS and UTS decrease by 10 MPa between them while TEL is similar.
The citing text states that MHT has the larger d_eff of 7.31 μm and slightly lower YS, UTS and TEL than S1050, declining by 35, 37 and 4.6% respectively at 25 °C.
The citing text states the YS, UTS, TEL and impact energy values are summarised in Table 1, not in this figure.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress–strain curves (y: Engineering Stress/MPa 0–1200; x: Engineering Strain/% 0–60) with four solid curves: MHT (black), S1000 (red), S1050 (blue), S1100 (cyan). Red/blue reach the highest plateau near 1100 MPa, black MHT ends earliest (~50% strain), cyan S1100 peaks just below 1000 MPa but extends to ~60%. A small grey-shaded inset drawing of a tensile specimen is present in the lower-middle region.

True Stress / Strain Hardening Rate (MPa, 0–2500) versus True Strain (0.0–0.5). Solid lines are the true-stress curves for MHT, S1000, S1050 and S1100; dashed/dotted lines are the corresponding strain-hardening-rate curves, which drop sharply at very low strain, rise to a hump near 2000 MPa around strain 0.2–0.25, then fall. Three regimes are labelled with roman numerals I, II and III.
